bibliographic.title: Presenting an International Entrepreneurship Model: A Case Study of ECO Member Countries
bibliographic.authors: Mojgan Haji Ghazi, Mohammad Mehdi Mazaheri Tehrani, Fereydoun Rahnamay Roodposhti
bibliographic.venue: Journal of New Approaches in Management and Marketing
bibliographic.citation_apa: Haji Ghazi, M., Mazaheri Tehrani, M. M., & Rahnamay Roodposhti, F. (2024). Presenting an International Entrepreneurship Model: A Case Study of ECO Member Countries. Journal of New Approaches in Management and Marketing, 3(2), 227-250. https://doi.org/10.22034/jnamm.2025.550465.1171

methodology.method_family: systematic data-based theory (grounded theory) with semi-structured interviews; factor analysis and structural equation modeling (SEM)
methodology.study_design: mixed-methods case study of ECO member countries
methodology.sample_description: 15 academic and executive experts interviewed until theoretical saturation; 323 managers randomly selected from 2035 managers of knowledge-based companies in the Export Development and Technology Exchange Corridor
methodology.sector: international entrepreneurship and knowledge-based companies in ECO member countries
methodology.technology_context: general references to technological infrastructure and digital platforms for regional entrepreneurship; no LLM, generative AI, or conversational systems

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study addresses international entrepreneurship modeling in ECO member countries and contains no discussion of LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, or governance of AI in regulated environments.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Matches on terms such as governance, legal, policy, transparency, and institutional refer to regional entrepreneurship policy-making, administrative barriers, and economic institutions—not conversational AI governance. Python triage flagged foundational_contextual due to keyword overlap, but full-text evidence shows the article is outside the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is unambiguous; no LLM, chatbot, agent, RAG, guardrails, or regulated AI governance content appears in the provided text.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects methodological quality for the entrepreneurship study as reported; validity confirmed by experts and Cronbach's alpha; qualitative analysis with MAXQDA and quantitative SEM with AMOS. Ethics and study limitations are not described in the provided excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: Although the entrepreneurship study appears internally coherent for its own aims, it provides no evidence relevant to conversational governance of LLM-based systems in regulated contexts.

coding.subtheme: Institutional and policy governance for cross-border entrepreneurship
concepts: Entrepreneurship Development Based on Multilevel Convergence
regional entrepreneurship policy model at three levels

synthesis.main_claim: International entrepreneurship in ECO member countries can be modeled through multi-level convergence linking contextual, causal, intervention, strategy, and consequence factors across macro, meso, and micro levels.
synthesis.contribution: Presents a mixed-methods indigenous model of entrepreneurship development with practical strategies for policymakers, economic institutions, and knowledge-based companies entering global markets.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central and supporting evidence; institutional governance and legal-policy content pertains to regional entrepreneurship, not conversational AI governance in regulated LLM systems.

evidence.claim: Article topic is international entrepreneurship in ECO countries, not AI or conversational systems
evidence.excerpt: The aim of the present study was to provide a comprehensive model for international entrepreneurship in ECO member countries.

evidence.claim: Mixed-methods design with expert interviews and manager survey
evidence.excerpt: A mixed research method was used: in the qualitative part, data were collected and analyzed using systematic data-based theory and interviews with 15 academic and executive experts

evidence.claim: Quantitative sample of 323 managers analyzed with SEM
evidence.excerpt: in the quantitative part, 323 managers were selected from 2035 managers of knowledge-based companies in the Export Development and Technology Exchange Corridor by random sampling

evidence.claim: Governance term refers to regional policy-making in entrepreneurship, not AI governance
evidence.excerpt: macro (regional policy-making and governance), meso (inter-organizational networks) and micro (individual skills and capabilities)

evidence.claim: Legal and policy content concerns administrative entrepreneurship barriers
evidence.excerpt: intervening conditions including administrative and bureaucratic challenges, legal and policy constraints and cultural and social barriers were identified

evidence.claim: Transparency discussed as lack of legal transparency in business registration
evidence.excerpt: Lengthy company registration processes, lack of legal transparency, sudden policy changes

Its main components include contextual factors (regional capacity building), causal factors (strategic context building), intervention factors (challenge management), strategies (operational framework), and consequences (sustainable development)

evidence.claim: Multi-level convergence is the central theoretical structure
evidence.excerpt: the international entrepreneurship model in ECO is based on multi-level convergence (macro, meso, and micro)

evidence.claim: No LLM, generative AI, or conversational technology mentioned in provided text
evidence.excerpt: obstacles such as weak institutional coordination, limited access to capital, ineffective support policies, insufficient use of new technologies, and lack of regional entrepreneurial networks
